summary: ZERO now runs natively on Linux, with packages for Linux Mint, Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora, and an AppImage for every distribution.
changes: Linux: .deb (Linux Mint, Ubuntu, Debian), .rpm (Fedora) and AppImage packages, with a menu entry and icon.
Settings > Linux: your system, sound server, display server and GPU at a glance, with checks and a report you can export without any personal data.
Linux updates follow how ZERO was installed: the AppImage replaces itself after a self-test and keeps a backup, and .deb or .rpm packages open in your system's installer, which asks for consent.
Plugins now show whether they work fully, partly or not at all on your system, and plugins can declare which systems they support.
improvements: GameDetection recognizes native Linux games and Windows games running through Steam Proton or Wine.
The screen share picker says when system sound cannot be shared (on Linux).
Logs and reports hide Linux home folder names as well as Windows user names.
